datasets.events_labeled: present (2774 events) — not yet scored by this build

conventions.crash_lead_h: hours from flag to dump (crash break / first close <=70% of peak); negative = after
conventions.early_window: tape rules: first 300 Nansen-indexed DEX trades (Nansen indexes pump.fun tokens from DEX migration, so for crashed tokens this is often at/after the curve peak); hourly rules: first 48 bars
conventions.era_matched: core50 subset created >= 2026-09-09 (crashed core50 is dominated by one Oct-10 launch batch)

rows.name: Per-token active-window filter
rows.status_why: built on hourly GT volume (rolling 7d per-token window, cohort prior when <72h history). Crashed tokens die within hours, so the token-level row is mostly untestable for them; the real test is event-level precision across every dump/pump alert bar in the full catalog.
rows.explain: Every token has hours when it actually trades (Asia vs US open). A sudden dump/pump bar that happens outside the hours that carry 60% of its own recent volume is more often noise. The filter discounts alerts outside the token's window and we measure how many false alerts that removes vs how many true ones it keeps.

extra.alert_def: 1h close-to-close <= -15% (dump) / >= +15% (pump) with volume >= 2x trailing-24h median; TRUE if within next 24h low <= -20% (dump) / high >= +20% (pump) from alert close
extra.window_def: smallest set of UTC hours carrying >=60% of the token's trailing-168h volume (max 12h); cohort prior (patterns_hours baseline) when <72 bars
extra.smart_money_note: Nansen-labelled smart/fund/KOL trades in the cached launch tapes; too few per token to learn a per-token SM window, shown as a global prior

rows.name: Vol compression before catalyst
rows.status_why: built: compression detector + event study on memecoin hourly and 246 majors daily; catalyst conditioning (DefiLlama unlock cliffs, grok_signals news) is live-only because there is no free historical catalyst calendar. Crashed test tokens die before a multi-week window exists (untestable).
rows.explain: When a coin's realized volatility sinks to its lowest level in weeks right before a known event (unlock, listing, upgrade, news), a large move often follows. The rule flags the squeeze; the event study checks whether big moves really are more likely after a squeeze than at other times, and which direction they break.

hourly_event_study.def: compressed = 24h realized vol at its 14-day low (6h steps); expansion = |max move| >= 30% within 72h

daily_majors_event_study.def: compressed = 7d realized vol <= min of prior 42 days; expansion = |max move| >= 20% within 14d; 246 CoinGecko majors, 365d

rows.name: Rich vs peers (mcap / cumulative volume) → mean reversion
rows.status_why: memecoins have no revenue/TVL, so the backtest uses the closest free proxy: market cap per $ of cumulative traded volume vs age-matched peers (>=3x the peer median = rich). FDV/TVL and FDV/fees vs DefiLlama category peers are computed for majors (live flags + 90d-back test in research/patternlab_ext/fairvalue_majors.py).
rows.explain: If a token is priced far above comparable projects for what it actually does (fees, TVL, or for memecoins: trading activity per $ of market cap), it tends to drift back toward the peer level. Rich = at least 3x the peer median.

majors.def: mcap/TVL vs DefiLlama category median 90d ago (>=3x rich, <=1/3 cheap); outcome = 90d return vs cross-sectional median

rows.name: Cheap vs peers (mcap / cumulative volume <= 1/3 peer median)
rows.status_why: mirror of 40 (undervalued side) — tested as a pump predictor
rows.explain: A token trading at a third of what peers with similar activity are worth may re-rate upward.

live_flags.name: Symbiosis
live_flags.why: mcap/TVL 0.24 vs Cross Chain Bridge median 1.63

rows.name: Stealth accumulation (no socials, rising on-chain activity)
rows.status_why: core50: new unique traders per 10-min bucket from cached Nansen launch tapes (Spearman rho>=0.5 and rising) while the token has no Twitter/Telegram/website yet (profile_delay_h honoured). full: 4 consecutive rising hourly volumes with |price| < 25% and no socials. No paid X reads: "social volume" = presence of any social channel, since historical mention counts for memecoins are not free.
rows.explain: Wallet count and activity keep climbing while nobody is talking about the token yet. That usually means early buyers are building positions quietly before the crowd shows up.

rows.name: Wallet rotation / closed loop (same wallets cycling 3-4 tokens)
rows.status_why: core50: wallets in the first 300 pre-peak trades (cached Nansen tapes) that also trade 3-12 other test tokens (wallets in >12 = routers/infra, excluded). Flag = >=10% of early traders are rotators and >=5 of them. full: top-holder overlap (DB snapshot taken after the peak, so post-hoc only).
rows.explain: The same group of wallets keeps jumping between the same few tokens: buying one, dumping into the next. That is a closed loop or a farming community, and the price is held up by the group rather than new buyers.

rows.name: Sybil buy bundle (>=5 wallets, same size +-5%, within 2 s)
rows.status_why: cached Nansen launch tapes, first 300 indexed trades
rows.explain: Many different wallets buying almost exactly the same amount within two seconds is one operator spreading a buy over sybil wallets (bundled launch or incentive farming). They usually exit together.

rows.name: Airdrop / points farming then dump
rows.status_why: wraps lib/airdrops.js (Airdrop Desk: farms, dilution, value estimates). Not testable on the 50-token set: pump.fun memecoins have no airdrop/points program. Proposal: Nansen tgm/who-bought-sold on claim day for airdropped majors (1 credit/token) to measure claimer dump share.
rows.explain: Wallets that farmed points/airdrops tend to sell on claim; a high share of claimers selling in the first days predicts weak price.

rows.name: Governance: whale votes / Snapshot / delegation changes
rows.status_why: wraps lib/socialalt.js governance-forum feed (Discourse hot topics: emissions, treasury, unlock votes). Snapshot vote-level whale share and delegation changes need per-DAO token mapping; memecoins in the test set have no governance, so no backtest (not-feasible on test set).
rows.explain: Big holders voting for emissions/treasury moves or re-delegating right before a vote often precede sell pressure. Flags hot governance threads about issuance/treasury/unlocks.

live_flags.why: HSP-XXX: Establish a 24-Month Issuance Ramp to a 1.6% Target Rate Of NEAR Token Emissions (23 posts)
NEST: tying the buyback threshold to the approved budget (7 posts)
Transfer 1,700 ETH from the Treasury to the Arbitrum Developer Guild & ATMC’s ETH Treasury (1 posts)

rows.name: Staking flows: large unstakes / LST & restaking outflows before dumps
rows.status_why: test-set memecoins have no staking; for majors the free data (validator/LST contract events) needs per-protocol indexers. Nansen could cover it (tgm/flows on LST tokens, ~1-5 credits/token) but there is no labelled staking-dump event set to backtest on, so it stays a proposal (est. 40-100 credits for 20 majors x 2 windows).
rows.explain: Large holders unstaking (with an unbonding delay) signals intention to sell when the coins unlock.

rows.name: Contract admin powers (mint/freeze/fee/hook/owner/proxy/hidden owner/selfdestruct/unverified)
rows.status_why: wraps lib/contractscan.js (EVM: proxy, owner, hidden owner, fee switches, selfdestruct, unverified bytecode, honeypot sim; Solana: mint/freeze authority, Token-2022 transfer fee/hook). Static snapshot (flag_t = creation). Proxy-upgrade / timelock / owner-change EVENTS over time need event logs per contract: not in scope of the free scan (proposal).
rows.explain: If the team can still mint, freeze, change fees, swap the contract implementation or hides an owner, they can rug at will. Checked on every test token the scanner covers.

rows.name: Mutable metadata (update authority kept)
rows.status_why: contractscan Solana metadata check
rows.explain: The deployer can still change the token's name/logo/links: weak sign of control.

rows.name: Mint or freeze authority not revoked (research DB)
rows.status_why: research DB mint_auth/freeze_auth
rows.explain: Unrevoked mint/freeze authority lets the team print tokens or freeze holders.

rows.name: Compiler-version anomalies / CREATE2-vanity deployers
rows.status_why: test set is pump.fun SPL tokens: one shared audited program, no per-token compiler or CREATE2. For EVM tokens contractscan already exposes unverified/proxy; compiler-version + vanity checks need verified source metadata from explorers (Etherscan key) — proposal.
rows.explain: Odd compiler versions or vanity CREATE2 addresses are sometimes used to dress up or redeploy rug templates.

rows.name: Behavioural fingerprint: same odd buy size reused by >=3 wallets
rows.status_why: cached Nansen launch tapes. KYC-linked clustering is NOT possible from public data; this is behavioural fingerprinting from on-chain amount habits (non-round SOL sizes to 4 significant digits) and timing.
rows.explain: Bots and multi-wallet operators reuse the same unusual buy size (e.g. 0.4137 SOL). Three or more wallets sharing it are probably one entity.

rows.name: Funding-source clustering (first funder / related wallets)
rows.status_why: covered by Pattern Lab #33 (first-buyer RPC age + funder) and #36 (same deployer bundle creates) and patterns detector 2 (fresh-wallet clusters, research/patterns_wallets.py) — not duplicated. Cross-chain clustering by funding source needs bridge-tx resolution (patterns detector 5 has it for Relay).
rows.explain: Wallets funded by the same source within minutes, then buying the same token, are one actor.

rows.name: Block trade: single sell >= 10% of cumulative volume
rows.status_why: cached Nansen launch tapes
rows.explain: One sell that is a large slice of all volume so far is an insider/whale distribution print.

rows.name: CEX deposit flows before the peak (dev/top holders → CEX)
rows.status_why: wraps patterns detector 3 (research/patterns_nansen.py: Nansen tgm/transfers include_cex + deployer transactions; and patterns_flows.py free RPC). Numbers re-scored both directions here.
rows.explain: Insiders moving tokens to an exchange usually sell. In this sample the opposite showed up: CEX-linked activity before the peak is a sign of a token big enough to reach CEX users.

rows.name: Stablecoin mint/burn spikes
rows.status_why: wraps lib/stables.js (chain-level mint/burn + velocity; backtest in stables.json backtest_summary: 44 tests, no Bonferroni survivor). Market-level, not token-level: no per-token backtest on the memecoin set.
rows.explain: Large stablecoin mints onto a chain bring buying power; burns drain it.

rows.name: OTC desk / market-maker flows
rows.status_why: wraps lib/otcflow.js (labelled OTC/MM wallets on Ethereum). Majors-only; dark-pool data does not exist publicly for crypto (not-feasible).
rows.explain: Tokens moving from OTC desks or market makers to exchanges precede supply hitting the book.

rows.name: Options flow: put/call ratio (Derive public data)
rows.status_why: live put/call OI ratio per underlying from the Derive snapshot (lib/derive.js). No option markets exist for the memecoin test set, and no free historical P/C series long enough to backtest (Deribit history is paid) — live only.
rows.explain: Very high put/call means hedging or bearish positioning; very low means crowded speculative longs. Both are contrarian warnings at extremes.

rows.name: Theme crowding: >=3 same-theme launches in the prior 24h
rows.status_why: research DB themes (topic model on token names/descriptions, narratives_taxonomy) + creation times across all 757 DB tokens
rows.explain: When the same meme theme is launched again and again within a day, the narrative is saturated and copies tend to die fast.

rows.name: Sentiment velocity & divergence from price
rows.status_why: wraps lib/sentiment.js + lib/narratives.js + grok signals (read-only data/grok_signals.json, no new Grok spend). Historical sentiment is only free for majors (Wikipedia-attention proxy, 36 tokens: no reliable edge, see sentiment_history.json); memecoin social history needs paid X reads (not used).
rows.explain: Fast-rising hype while price stalls (or panic while price holds) is a divergence that often resolves against the crowd.

extra.majors_backtest: Wikipedia-attention proxy, 36 tokens since 2015-17: euphoric spikes (z>=3 after a +10% week) were followed by a negative 14d return 52% of the time vs 54% for all +10% weeks (n=355, perm p=0.744, no reliable edge); panic spikes after a -10% week rebounded 52% vs 46% (n=120, perm p=0.076, no reliable edge); year-low attention after a down month rose over 30d 43% vs 45% (n=680, perm p=0.632, no reliable edge).

rows.name: Influence propagation speed / diffusion
rows.status_why: needs post-level timelines and follower graphs (paid X reads — not allowed). Free Telegram/Discord/RSS mentions (socialalt) have no reliable timestamps per account to measure diffusion.
rows.explain: How fast a token mention spreads from a few accounts to many.

rows.name: MEV sandwich density (same wallet buy→sell within 2 s around others)
rows.status_why: cached Nansen launch tapes; wraps lib/mev.js heuristics (terminal-swap sandwich audit). Jito tip anomalies are Pattern Lab #23 (not duplicated).
rows.explain: Heavy sandwiching means bots are farming the order flow: retail gets bad fills and the chart is inflated by bot volume.

rows.name: Priority-fee / tip anomalies, block-inclusion timing
rows.status_why: Jito tips in the first 2 s are Pattern Lab #23; block-0 sniping is rule 44 here. Priority-fee distributions for every trade would need ~15k getTransaction calls on public RPC — not run.
rows.explain: Insiders pay unusually high priority fees to land in the launch block.

rows.name: Gas griefing, reorgs, L2 sequencer downtime
rows.status_why: Solana has no reorgs at finality and no sequencer; gas griefing is an EVM concept. Base sequencer downtime affects 11 Base tokens in the full set only and is market-wide (no token-level variance).
rows.explain: Network incidents freeze exits and cause liquidation cascades.

rows.name: Code similarity to known rug/honeypot contracts
rows.status_why: wraps contractscan_templates.json (EVM runtime-bytecode skeletons vs our confirmed honeypots; clone families in contractscan_corr.json). Solana pump.fun tokens all use the same SPL program, so code similarity has zero variance on the test set (not-feasible there).
rows.explain: A token whose bytecode skeleton matches previous rugs was probably made by the same kit.

rows.name: Audit-firm reputation, symbolic execution (slither/mythril), formal verification
rows.status_why: no test-set token has an audit; slither/mythril need verified Solidity source (not available for SPL tokens; most EVM memecoins unverified) — contractscan already simulates honeypots at bytecode level. Formal-verification results are only published for large DeFi protocols.
rows.explain: Audits by reputable firms and clean symbolic-execution reports lower (not remove) rug risk.

rows.name: No website / docs 1h after creation (and website changes)
rows.status_why: presence tested (time-aware, profile_delay_h) from research DB has_website. Wayback/DNS/hash diffs of project sites need the URL history per token; DexScreener profile URLs are not stored historically for the test set (proposal: daily hash of live-feed token sites).
rows.explain: Projects that never set up a site/docs — or that quietly change them — are lower-effort or preparing a pivot.

rows.name: NFT community crossover
rows.status_why: no free mapping from memecoin holders to NFT collections on Solana without paid indexers (Nansen NFT endpoints are not in our allowed price list).
rows.explain: Tokens adopted by an existing NFT community have a built-in holder base.

rows.name: Referral / points program launches attracting mercenary capital
rows.status_why: no structured free feed of referral launches; would need scraping project announcements (paid X).
rows.explain: Referral programs pull in mercenary wallets that leave when rewards end.

rows.name: Deployer sells in the early tape
rows.status_why: cached Nansen launch tapes (first 300 indexed trades)
rows.explain: The deployer wallet selling in the first trades is the classic soft rug.

rows.name: Block-0 snipers: >=20% of early buy volume in the first 5 s
rows.status_why: cached Nansen launch tapes (first 300 indexed trades)
rows.explain: Wallets that buy within seconds of trading opening are usually insiders/bots who dump into the first wave of buyers.

rows.name: Flippers: >=40% of first 100 buyers sell within 10 min
rows.status_why: cached Nansen launch tapes (first 300 indexed trades)
rows.explain: If most early buyers flip within minutes, nobody is holding: the token has no base.

rows.name: Buyer concentration: top-5 wallets >=50% of early buy volume
rows.status_why: cached Nansen launch tapes (first 300 indexed trades)
rows.explain: A handful of wallets doing most of the buying controls the price and the exit.

rows.name: Smart-money / KOL / high-balance wallets present early (>=2)
rows.status_why: cached Nansen launch tapes (first 300 indexed trades)
rows.explain: Labelled skilled or well-funded wallets buying early often front-run a real move.

rows.name: Sell ramp: sell share in last quarter >=55% and +15pp vs first quarter
rows.status_why: cached Nansen launch tapes (first 300 indexed trades)
rows.explain: Selling takes over as the early phase goes on.

rows.name: Round-trip wash: wallets with >=3 buys and >=3 sells carry >=20% of volume
rows.status_why: cached Nansen launch tapes (first 300 indexed trades)
rows.explain: Volume made by the same wallets buying and selling back and forth is fake activity.

rows.name: Bot-dominated tape: >=50% of trades by labelled trading bots
rows.status_why: cached Nansen launch tapes (first 300 indexed trades)
rows.explain: Tapes dominated by Telegram trading-bot users are fast-money and churn quickly.

rows.name: Serial deployers trading it (>=3 wallets labelled as other tokens' deployers)
rows.status_why: cached Nansen launch tapes (first 300 indexed trades)
rows.explain: Wallets that launch memecoins for a living buying each other's launches = farming circle.

rows.name: Wallet velocity: >=150 distinct wallets in the first 30 min
rows.status_why: cached Nansen launch tapes (first 300 indexed trades)
rows.explain: Lots of distinct wallets arriving fast means real distribution.

rows.name: Large median buy (>= $50)
rows.status_why: cached Nansen launch tapes (first 300 indexed trades)
rows.explain: Bigger typical tickets = real money rather than dust bots.

rows.name: Mayhem-mode program participation (>=10 trades)
rows.status_why: cached Nansen launch tapes (first 300 indexed trades)
rows.explain: pump.fun Mayhem-mode (agent-driven) trading in the early tape.

rows.name: Activity collapse: trades in minutes 10-20 < 30% of minutes 0-10
rows.status_why: cached Nansen launch tapes (first 300 indexed trades)
rows.explain: Interest disappearing right after launch.

rows.name: Repeat deployer: >=3 prior launches
rows.status_why: research DB static fields (flag_t = creation)
rows.explain: Deployers who launch many tokens rarely support any of them.

rows.name: No socials 1h after creation (no X, Telegram or website)
rows.status_why: research DB static fields (flag_t = creation)
rows.explain: A token with no community channels has nobody to defend it. (time-aware: DexScreener profile_delay_h honoured so later-added socials do not leak.)

rows.name: Fast bonding curve (<10 min to graduate)
rows.status_why: research DB static fields (flag_t = creation)
rows.explain: Graduating in minutes is usually bundled/sniped buying, not organic demand.

rows.name: Asia-hours launch (00-08 UTC)
rows.status_why: research DB static fields (flag_t = creation)
rows.explain: Launches while the US sleeps have thinner books.

rows.name: DEX boost paid within 1h of creation
rows.status_why: research DB static fields (flag_t = creation)
rows.explain: Paying for DexScreener boosts right at launch means a team spending on promotion (time-aware: boosts bought after the run are excluded).
